To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
lactosaminated HSA–ara‐A conjugates are taken up by rat hepatocytes via endocytosis and released their ara‐A moiety into lysosomes.
the coupling of ara-AMP to lactosamine-modified human serum albumin leads to a conjugate with a predominantly monomeral structure that is stable in buffer and in blood plasma.
the antiviral agent ara‐AMP is covalently coupled to a carrier molecule, lactosaminated HSA, and the resulting conjugate specifically binds to the liver via the asialoglyco‐protein receptor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new antiviral strategies.
the design of a new drug carrier system for the antiviral agent ara‐AMP, which can be used to deliver this drug specifically to hepatocytes.
the design and development of new drugs for the treatment of viral infections.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
lactosaminated carrier proteins can be used to target ara‐AMP to hepatocytes in vivo.
the lactosaminated HSA–ara‐A conjugate is a promising candidate for the treatment of viral hepatitis.
the coupling of ara-AMP to lactosamine-modified albumin results in a specific carrier for hepatocyte targeting of the antivirus drug ara-AMP.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
lactosaminated HSA–ara‐ AMP9 is an efficient carrier molecule for ara‐A to the liver.
we were able to show that a water‐soluable antiviral agent could be coupled to lactosamin‐ated albumin in a stable manner and could be taken up in hepatocytes.
we have developed a method for conjugation of ara‐AMP to a carrier molecule (lac27‐ HSA–ara‐ AMP9) which leads to selective uptake in rat and man hepatocytes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have developed a method for the conjugation of the antivirally active drug ara‐AMP with lactosaminated HSA.
the coupling of the antivirus agent ara‐AMP to the carrier molecule HSA resulted in an efficient and selective delivery of the antivirally active components to rat hepatocytes.
the galactose receptor can be exploited for the targeted delivery of nucleoside analogs to hepatocytes.
